_comment: The `meshweaver` ACR retention tasks, as they exist in Azure. Read back with
`az acr task show`, 2026-09-07 (MeshWeaver#3438).
🚨 THESE TASKS ARE CLOUD-ONLY. `az acr task show` returns an `EncodedTask` with
`contextPath: null` — the YAML is stored base64-encoded inside Azure with no source
repository — and an org-wide code search for `purge-old-images` returns zero hits outside
this repository's doc pages. This directory is the record, NOT the source of truth: nothing
deploys from it. `.github/scripts/acr-retention-tasks.sh verify` is what relates the two, and
`… apply` is a maintainer-run command that pushes this record back onto the registry.
Why the record exists at all: the definitions carry the reasoning from two incidents
(Memex#122, MeshWeaver#3438) in comments that live in exactly one place — inside a base64
blob in a cloud resource nobody diffs. A `az acr task update` from any laptop replaces them
silently and completely.
`schedule`/`status`/`timeout` here are ASSERTED by `verify`; the remaining fields are
provenance and are printed, not compared.
🚨 2026-09-12: `purge-old-images` is DISABLED. Roland ordered the purge paused while the
protection is incomplete (Memex#219); measured the same morning with `az acr task list`, both
tasks read `status: Disabled`. The pause is the MITIGATION and MeshWeaver#4081 is the FIX, so
#4081 is the precondition for turning the task back on rather than a race against it. Quote no
deletion date while `pause` below is in force: there is no live clock, and a date that has
silently stopped being true is what the next reader acts on.
🚨 A DISABLED TASK STILL SHOWS AN ENABLED TIMER. `az acr task list` reports
`status: Disabled` on the task while its `trigger.timerTriggers[0].status` still reads
`Enabled` at `0 3 * * *`. Read the TASK's status; the trigger's is about the trigger.

tasks.name: purge-old-images
notes: 🚨 DISABLED 2026-09-12 — see the top-level `pause` block. This was `Enabled` at `0 3 * * *`; every note below describes the policy it runs WHEN RE-ENABLED.
ONE task, TWO steps: a 30d step over the CI image repositories, and a separate 30d step
for memex-portal. The filter lists stay SEPARATE even at one window — they are not
symmetric (mw-plugin-test is unique to the first, memex-portal to the second), and a
union-merge would silently retune one of them the next time either window moves.
decided rule is at least 30 days by age with NO build-count quota; #3843 and #3846
clamped the bundle store and the assembly cache to it and left the registry out in as
many words. `lock-pinned-digests.py --check-retention-record` now asserts it on every
pull request. See `recordAheadOfRegistry` below: the live task still carries the old
window, and this record is what `apply` would push.
Both steps share ONE 3600 s task budget; the per-step `timeout` is a per-step ceiling.
🚨 NEITHER STEP PASSES `--include-locked`, and that is the whole of the pin protection:
`acr purge` skips locked manifests by default. Adding that flag would delete every

tasks.name: purge-old-ci-releases
notes: SUPERSEDED and DISABLED, not deleted — its filter list was folded into
purge-old-images's two steps. Kept as the record of the Memex#122 reasoning it carries,
and so that re-enabling it is a visible act rather than a rediscovery.
Do not re-enable it: two divergent lists is the defect #3438 named.

recordAheadOfRegistry.what: purge-old-images.yaml step 1 records `--ago 30d` with no `--keep`; the live (disabled) task still carries `--ago 7d --keep 10`.
recordAheadOfRegistry.why: #3842's decided rule — at least 30 days by age, no build-count quota — was landed in the bundle store (#3843) and the assembly cache (#3846) and explicitly NOT in the registry. The record is what `acr-retention-tasks.sh apply` pushes, so stating the decided window here is what makes re-enabling the task install a window somebody chose. Nothing was applied: this is a record change, not a registry change.
recordAheadOfRegistry.clearedBy: the next `acr-retention-tasks.sh apply` — after which `verify` finds no drift on these tasks and reds on THIS declaration being stale, which is how it expires rather than rotting.

pause.measured: az acr task list --registry meshweaver — purge-old-images status=Disabled (timer trigger still Enabled at 0 3 * * *)
pause.reason: Roland ordered the purge paused while artifact protection is incomplete: the fleet's tag references, the platform manifests under every locked index, and one production instance's running index were all unprotected (MeshWeaver#3438).
pause.reEnableWhen: lock-pinned-digests is green on a fleet whose tag references and index closures are locked — MeshWeaver#4081. Re-enabling before that restores the exposure the pause exists to hold off.
